title: The Altitude Where Sound Forgets to Echo

features.name: transmission tower
features.desc-on-touch: it broadcasts down to the flatlands. nothing broadcasts back. the signal goes out but the return path is broken; or worse, it listens forever

features.name: acoustic void
features.desc-on-touch: the air is so thin that sound dies instantly; radio waves persist, but if you speak here, your words disappear before they materialize

features.name: log books weathered
features.desc-on-touch: station records of radio reception, gardening conditions, cloud movements. later entries describe the same day over and over, with slight variations. all dated correctly

features.name: wind installation
features.desc-on-touch: a device meant to measure wind speed. the needle jitters in agitation; sometimes it reads negative numbers; sometimes it points to places that have no direction

features.name: silent field
features.desc-on-touch: the highest part of the peak, where even the archive's broadcast becomes inaudible. standing here, you hear only your own blood. the world continues elsewhere, wordless

inscription: at this height, the air forgets how to carry sound; what was once silence becomes the first true word

file.name: PeakStation_GardenLog_Repeat_Days_1979_1985.txt
file.note: weather observations alternate with gardening notes; radio reception logs describe songs from stations that may or may not exist; the pattern is calm, methodical, unstoppable

exits.label: back down to the acoustic ridge where echoes still argue
toward the peak's invisible summit, higher than breathing allows
down the western slope, toward the settlement where this broadcast once arrived with clarity
